claims.subject: sculptural_surface
claims.value: Classical Greek architectural and marble sculpture could be painted; surviving bare white marble does not prove an originally unpainted surface.
claims.confidence_reason: Supported by cited museum/heritage/specialist evidence at the stated scope.
claims.interpretation: Treat white-marble museum appearance as an artifact-state outcome, not an automatic in-period truth.
prompt_implications: For newly created or in-period Classical marble, allow evidence-aware polychromy or pigment details when appropriate. For conserved/excavated states, largely bare marble with surviving pigment traces can be plausible while preserving the distinction from original appearance.
claims.survival_bias: Weathering, cleaning, burial, and conservation can remove or reduce ancient paint; present white marble is not identical to original surface intent.

claims.subject: bronze_fabrication
claims.value: Large ancient Greek bronzes were commonly produced through hollow lost-wax casting, often in separately cast sections joined and cold-worked.
claims.confidence_reason: Supported by cited museum/heritage/specialist evidence at the stated scope.
claims.interpretation: This is a fabrication system, not merely a bronze color.
prompt_implications: For bronze sculpture, show cast metal logic: plausible joins, chased/cold-worked details, controlled wall/thickness implications, metal inlays where appropriate, and metallic surface response.

claims.subject: survival_bias
claims.value: Few large ancient bronzes survive because valuable metal was often melted down; Roman marble copies can dominate modern visual memory of Greek sculptural types.
claims.confidence_reason: Supported by cited museum/heritage/specialist evidence at the stated scope.
claims.interpretation: Do not infer original material prevalence from surviving museum counts alone.
prompt_implications: When reconstructing a living ancient sculptural environment, do not default every Greek statue to white marble merely because more marble copies survive.
claims.survival_bias: Survival is selective: bronze was recyclable and often lost, while marble copies survived differently.
